claim: Nell marries Hugh Carrow.
Nell's first baby, Joyce, dies.
Nell lives in the House of Dreams at Seven Gulls Harbour.
Nell's son James Obed, called Kit, is born.
Nell lives at Hollowmere in Glen St. Agnes.
Hugh becomes a doctor at Seven Gulls Harbour.
Hugh marries Nell Harcourt.
Nell names her son James Obed partly after Obed.
Edmund is a dreamy boy who loves poetry.
Grace Ashdown dares Edmund to ride a pig through Main Street.
Edmund hates Dan Coyle.
Tessa is the youngest of the Carrow children.
Captain Saul dies soon after his life-book is published.
Captain Saul is a high-souled, simple-minded old man with iron-gray hair.
Captain Saul's surname is Garrick.
Captain Saul keeps a life-book.
Captain Saul tells Nell about lost Margaret.
Lorna was pressured by her mother into marrying Rufus Vane.
Lorna and Adrian Treleaven are to be married at Christmas.
Ambrose Kerr has turned himself into a kind of dime museum freak.
Miss Winifred has a chronic spite against men and Methodists.
Miss Winifred marries Ambrose Kerr.
Rufus Vane went on a voyage to Havana with his cousin Laurence Vane.
The man believed to be Rufus Vane is his cousin Laurence Vane.
Rufus Vane died of yellow fever in Cuba.
Adrian Treleaven is a newspaper man and a grandson of the schoolmaster who built the house.
Tabitha Pratt works as maid-of-all-work at the little house.
Tabitha worships Nell as young Mrs. Doctor.
Mr. Ashdown is moony and absent-minded but a wonderful preacher.
Mr. Ashdown is a widower whose wife died four years ago.
Mr. Ashdown and Clementine Ainslie are to marry.
Ida Ashdown is ten years old.
Ida gives her father a letter from Clementine.
Rupert Ashdown collects toads, bugs and frogs.
Rupert gets a sore throat after getting wet in the Fern Hollow marsh.
Grace Ashdown dares Edmund Carrow to ride a pig.
Mary Stubbs eats ravenously at the manse.
Mary Stubbs lives with Miss Winifred.
Lionel Fairlie used to give a hundred dollars a year to the church.
Lionel Fairlie married Dinah Coyle to spite Harriet Ainslie.
Harriet Ainslie went about with Lionel Fairlie for two years.
Harriet Ainslie and Lionel Fairlie want to marry.
Clementine Ainslie has made a promise to her sister Harriet.
Clementine Ainslie's lover was lost at sea.
Kit suggests the manse children form a Good-Conduct Club.
